summary.headline: Cyient DLM Q2 FY27 revenue rose 26.5% YoY to INR3,931 million, with record INR28.1 billion order book, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.7%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 26.5% YoY to INR3,931 million and H1 revenue grew 30.2% to INR7,669 million. The order book hit an all-time high of INR28.1 billion, up about INR2.1 billion QoQ, with book-to-bill above 1.6x. EBITDA margin fell 135 bps YoY to 8.7% as sales, marketing and product development spend was expensed. Reported PAT of INR340 million included a one-time INR182 million earn-out reversal; normalized PAT was INR158 million, up 25.8% YoY.

financial_highlights.change: Includes one-time earn-out reversal of INR182 million

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 47% of Q2 revenue, growing 62% YoY.

segments.name: Product mix: Box build
segments.commentary: 27% of Q2 revenue, growing about 85-86% YoY; 3 new logos added in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 9% (high single digit); Shashank Jha's follow-up was answered as 9-10%.
From Q1 FY28 onward, management expects EBITDA margins in double digits; Krishna Bodanapu said FY28 margins could reach 10-plus percent from executing backlog without extra effort.
Revenue growth of 30-35% expected for FY27; H2 FY27 growth to be above 30%, though quarterly growth may vary.
Margin framework: 9-11% (phase 1, core), 11-13% (phase 2, FY27-FY29), 13-18% (phase 3, FY30 onward, electronic products).
No further sales and marketing cost additions planned until quarterly revenue doubles on a net new basis.
Management to update on AI data center and robotics opportunities by end of FY27.
capex_capacity: Product development and sales costs are fully expensed; none capitalized under current policy. Margin impact of these investments put at 100-150 bps.
Order book execution period is typically 18-24 months.
Semiconductor capital equipment work has been underway, with revenue in the last two quarters; ramp-up expected.
Altek Electronics integrated and renamed Cyient DLM Electronics, Inc. (US); sales team being built on the ground.
Build-to-spec (now electronic products) programs: 4 programs, close to $1 billion unweighted, 7-9 year contracts, production expected from FY29 with ramp from FY30.
demand_pricing: Order book INR28.1 billion, up from INR26 billion in Q1 and about INR5.2 billion YoY.

Unweighted bid pipeline above $1 billion (down from about $1.4 billion earlier; Krishna cited about $1.5 billion); expected win ratio about 40%, implying $400-500 million of order intake from the existing pipeline.
Q1 and Q2 order intake was close to INR600 crore; management expects similar in the next two quarters.
Revenue growth slowed to 26.5% in Q2 from about 35% in Q1, attributed to material availability, memory-market supply constraints, longer lead times and customer-site delays.
Export-led business: rest of world 93% of revenue, India 7%. Domestic build-to-spec opportunities being pursued.
Honeywell build-to-print program (Micro VCS/Atiun-related box build) in prototype and testing; production timing not stated precisely.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin decline was from one-off product development costs versus revenue mix, and what is the annual product development budget?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the investment impact is 100-150 bps, all expensed, and declined to give an annual product development budget.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajendra Velagapudi guided FY27 EBITDA margin to about 9%, high single digit, with double-digit margins from Q1 FY28 onward.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue lagging the order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited material procurement challenges; order book converts over 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin lower YoY, and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishna Bodanapu said gross and contribution margins are higher YTD; the drop is from sales and marketing costs now fully in SG&A with zero absorption, roughly 100-150 bps, and product development is not capitalized.

qa_highlights.question: What is the $1 billion B2S order book and when will it convert?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said four build-to-spec programs, close to $1 billion, are not yet in the order book; contracts partly signed, production from FY29-FY30, over 7-9 year terms.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Honeywell program involve liquid cooling?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajendra said it is a build-to-print box build with significant electronics, not liquid cooling, and a separate module.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin at 8.7% in Q2 versus 10% last year; FY27 guidance of about 9% depends on cost absorption and margin recovery.
Material shortages, memory-market constraints and longer lead times could keep delaying revenue conversion.
Growth guidance of 30-35% for FY27 versus 26.5% in Q2.
Reported PAT includes INR182 million one-time earn-out reversal; normalized figures are the better guide.
B2S/electronic products revenue depends on converting unweighted pipeline (~$1 billion) into contracts; production not before FY29-FY30.
Other income (about INR23 crore) includes forex and export incentives and varies quarter to quarter.
Management commitment to double-digit margins from FY28 and no further sales and marketing additions until quarterly revenue doubles.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order book, but defensive on margins; management repeatedly said the margin dip reflects deliberate sales and product development spend. Answers on pipeline size, product development budget and timing of B2S revenue were vague or deferred.
key_quotes: The reason why margins are really lower is 2 things. One is we've invested quite a bit in sales and marketing, all of which is now in the P&L, like in the SG&A, S&M or G&A.
So it's really -- net-net, if I may just clarify, the reason for the drop in margins by about 100 bps or so is because all the sales and marketing costs have been accounted for.
The order backlog is like a balance sheet, right? It's at a point in time. It's not like a P&L, which would be for a period.
So it's a constant addition. So you can't say that the order book or the -- sorry, the pipeline is for a period.

adds.what: Build-to-spec electronic products: 4 programs (close to $1 bn unweighted), production expected from FY29 with ramp from FY30

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% and H2 growth above 30%, backed by a record INR28.1bn order book (1.6x book-to-bill) and steady INR600 crore quarterly intake, though Q2 growth slowed to 26.5% on material and memory supply constraints; FY27 EBITDA margin was cut to about 9%, with no new physical capacity disclosed beyond build-to-spec programs starting FY29.
